transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because my sleep has been really broken for a long time. I go to bed exhausted, but I wake up at every little sound in the house, and then I’m up before the alarm. It feels like I never really rested.
Have you ever been through something very frightening or traumatic?
Not that I can think of, no. I mean, I’ve had hard times like most people, but nothing I’d call very frightening or traumatic.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different parts of your life, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?
I don’t think so. I mean, I worry about normal things, but I wouldn’t say it’s a lot of different things all the time. It’s not like I’m constantly going from one worry to another.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energetic or high and needed much less sleep than usual?
No, I don’t think so. I’ve never had a stretch where I felt unusually high or full of energy like that, or where I could get by on barely any sleep.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yes. Most days I feel pretty down… like the color’s gone out of things. Even when I’m with my family at Sunday dinner, or looking at art I used to really enjoy, it just feels flat. And sometimes I have to try hard not to tear up, even when there isn’t a clear reason.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

I’m not really sure how to answer that. I mean, some things don’t feel the same lately, but I don’t know if I’d say I’ve completely lost interest or pleasure. It’s more like… I notice things feel kind of dull sometimes.
How long have you been feeling down like this?
It’s been a little over two years, I think. It started around when my mother-in-law moved in with us, and it’s just kind of stayed that way since then.
During the past two years, have you felt down more days than not?

Yes… I’d say more days than not. Most days it’s like things feel drained of color, even if I’m with my family at Sunday dinner or looking at art I used to enjoy. And sometimes I’m fighting back tears without really knowing why.
During these past two years, has there ever been a stretch of two months or longer when you did not feel down?
No, I don’t think so. Since my mother-in-law moved in a little over two years ago, it’s been pretty constant. There might be better days, but not a whole two months where I felt okay.
Do you often feel badly about yourself?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I don’t think about it in those exact words all the time. Sometimes I feel like I’m not doing enough or I should be handling things better, but I don’t know if that’s the same as feeling badly about myself.
Do you often feel tired or low on energy?

Yes. By the time I’m done seeing my home-health clients and then come back and help at home, I feel worn out. My body just feels heavy, and even small things like charting my notes or folding laundry can feel like too much to push through.
Do you often feel hopeless?

Yes… a lot of days it feels like the color has gone out of things. Even when I’m with my family at Sunday dinner, or looking at art I used to really enjoy, it just feels flat. And sometimes I have to really work not to tear up, even when I don’t know exactly why.
Have you often had a poor appetite or been eating more than usual?

Yeah… more like I don’t have much appetite. I’ll cook or make food for everyone else and then just pick at it, or after work I’ll just have some toast because that’s all I can manage. I’ve noticed my clothes are fitting looser, and I’m not trying to lose weight.
At any point during the past two years, was there a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed nearly every day?

Yes. There have been stretches like that, definitely more than two weeks, where most days I just feel down. It’s like the color has gone out of things, even if I’m with my family at Sunday dinner or looking at art I used to enjoy. And I have to work hard not to tear up, even when I don’t really know why.
During these past two years, have you had trouble sleeping on most nights?

Yes. Most nights, really. I’ll be exhausted and fall into bed, but my sleep is broken. I wake up at every little noise in the house, and then I’m up before the alarm feeling like I didn’t rest at all.
Do you often have trouble concentrating?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I have my days where I’m distracted, like anybody, but I haven’t noticed it being a big problem or something that stands out.
Do you often have a hard time making decisions?
I don’t think so, not especially. I mean, I can go back and forth on things sometimes, but I haven’t noticed decision-making being a major problem for me.
When your mood feels a little better, do you still have the same trouble sleeping?
Yes, even when my mood lifts a bit, the sleep problem is still there. I’ll be really tired and go to bed, but I wake up at little noises, and then I’m up too early feeling like I didn’t really sleep.
Does your sleep problem make it hard for you to function during the day?

Yes. It does. I’m getting through the day, but it feels like I’m just barely keeping up. At work I’ve started falling behind on my client documentation, and I don’t really volunteer to help mentor the newer aides like I used to. By the time I get through the basics at work and then things at home, that’s about all I have in me.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?
I don’t really know how to answer that. I mean, I’ve felt worn down and discouraged, but I’m not sure I’d say I’ve been thinking about hurting myself.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports depressed mood more days than not for over 2 years without any symptom-free interval of 2 months or longer, consistent with persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia). Associated symptoms confirmed include low energy, poor appetite with weight loss, insomnia, and hopelessness. Although there have been periods of at least 2 weeks of more intense depressive symptoms, the chronicity and continuity of low mood favor F34.1 over a single depressive episode. Insomnia is clinically significant but occurs in the context of a chronic depressive syndrome, making it secondary rather than the primary diagnosis.
